messages:
anya: kicking off a soak test in staging to validate per-org and per-key rate limiting with burst windows. script: k6 --vus 200 --duration 30m targeting /v1/generate with short think times.
kevin: noted. are we using token-per-user or api-key-per-org for this run? last run had keys multiplexed across orgs.
sam: using api_key header. script rotates keys every 30s to simulate many clients. target config: per-key limit=60rps, per-org limit=1000rps, burst window=5s. sending bursts to validate fallback routing and quota enforcement.
maria: FYI from the earlier run: we saw 429 spikes but dashboard didn't show which limiter fired — per-key vs per-org ambiguous.
anya: can someone grep limiter logs? I suspect a sharding mismatch: when worker count changed we might hash keys to wrong shards, losing counters.
kevin: looking now. limiter logs show limiter_id=per_key shard=3 key=org:123:key:abcd counts incrementing but TTL looks suspiciously short. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:01Z] limiter=per_key key=org:123:key:abcd count=65 window=1s limit=60 ttl=500ms
```
sam: TTL 500ms is wrong — should be 60s per config. I think an env override from an earlier perf experiment wasn't reverted. :facepalm:
maria: that would explain counters evicting quickly and allowing unexpected bursts. can we confirm where TTL is coming from? config file or env?
kevin: config file /etc/rl/config.yaml has ttl_ms: 60000. but deploy has LIMTER_CACHE_TTL_MS=500 set in the systemd unit for rl-worker. someone must have left it in.
anya: ok that's the smoking gun. implications: when TTL is too short, the per-key counter disappears mid-window so bursts bypass intended throttles. rerun after fixing.
sam: patching unit file now and restarting rl-worker in staging. adding a short test: single-key steady 100rps for 2m should yield 429s if limiter works.
ops-bot: deploy started: rl-worker v2.3.4 -> v2.3.5 (config patch).
kevin: worker back up. starting the scripted run: ./scripts/burst_rotate.sh --keys=500 --rotate=30s --duration=20m --mix=bursty,steady
sam: enhancing the k6 script to capture response headers and emit x-rl-name and x-rl-reason so we can attribute 429s to per_key vs per_org. also logging x-rl-ttl to confirm proper TTL is applied.
maria: can we add a temporary grafana panel for this run showing: per-key 429 rate, per-org 429 rate, avg-token-ttl, and limiter-shard distribution? makes debugging easier.
anya: yes please. also add a slow-moving synthetic user that holds one key and does 100rps for 10m to validate per-key enforcement.
kevin: run started. quick log: 
```
[2026-03-15T16:05:10Z] synthetic:key=org:555:key:zzzz rps=100 status=429 x-rl-name=per_key x-rl-reason=rate_limit x-rl-ttl=60000
```
sam: results after 20m: aggregate looks good. per-key 429s align with expected thresholds, per-org only fired when aggregate >1000rps. no weird TTL evictions observed.
maria: can we make TTL an explicit field in the rollout UI? right now overrides are invisible; ops accidentally left a perf override in unit files. we need visibility.
anya: agree. create a console ticket to show "active env overrides" for rate-limiter settings and surface them on the rollout diff. that should prevent surprises.
kevin: filing ticket PLAT-7892: "Show active rate-limiter env overrides in rollout UX" — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAT-7892
sam: also adding a unit/integration test for parsing LIMTER_CACHE_TTL_MS and ensuring deploy tooling warns when non-default overrides are present.
anya: excellent. next step: schedule a 6h soak with mixed traffic (api keys, sessions, streaming) next week, and include an experiment to rotate worker count to validate shard remapping.
maria: noted. I'll draft the test plan and dashboard panels and share. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
